function: Learned joint control of per-stream transmit power (MRT/ZF directions), LED DC bias, RSMA common rates, and IRS element alignment, to maximize secrecy energy efficiency (p. 6-7).
system: Indoor VLC MISO downlink, visible light: 6 LEDs, 2 single-PD legitimate users, 1 eavesdropper, passive reflecting optical IRS with 16 mirror-like elements, RSMA (p. 3, 9).
method: DS-PPO reinforcement learning: actor and critic MLPs (2 hidden layers, 256 tanh units), dual on-/off-policy sampling, GAE, trained online by interaction for 1.5e7 steps (p. 8-10).
data_channel: Own simulated VLC channels: Lambertian LoS plus specular IRS NLoS in a 6x6x3 m room; users and Eve random on the ground; CSI assumed known (p. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Agent trained and evaluated in the same simulated room; sweeps of IRS elements, LUs, power budget, QoS threshold; no unseen-scenario test stated (p. 9-12).
baselines: PPO [48] and DDPG [49] (learned); epsilon-greedy search without neural networks; MRT-only beamforming design [50]; RSMA versus SDMA comparison (p. 10-11).
metrics: Secrecy energy efficiency (SEE), average reward, per-user achievable rate against QoS threshold, total power, and average time cost per step (p. 10-12).
complexity: Order O(sum of m_(p-1)*m_p over layers) (Remark 2, p. 9); time cost per step plotted; DS-PPO sacrifices less than 5% of time cost versus PPO (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 4: "the VLC channel gain can be determined based on the geometric position of the LED transmitters and the LU"; own Lambertian LoS plus specular NLoS model, no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured data
q2_support: p. 10: "Fig. 3 illustrates the training process curves of the proposed DS-PPO approach to show its convergence behaviors"; results are training curves and sweeps in the same simulated room, with no unseen scenario, band or dataset, and no transfer or fine-tuning
q3_support: p. 10: "In the ε-Greedy-based approach, the agent explores the action to maximize the achievable SEE in every time step"; p. 11: "although DDPG achieves remarkable advantages in terms of the faster convergence speed, the corresponding SEE is relatively low compared with DS-PPO and PPO approaches"
q4_support: p. 11: "DS-PPO sacrifices less than 5% of the time cost compared to PPO"
q5_support: p. 9: "In the simulations, the considered VLC network is deployed in a room"; self-simulated scenario, and no link to code or data anywhere in the paper
notes: Version read: arXiv v1 preprint (14 Nov 2024), 13 pages. The optical IRS (mirror-like reflecting elements, p. 3) counts as a RIS. Learned part: transmit power scaling, DC bias, common rates and relaxed IRS alignment; beam directions come from MRT/ZF closed forms (p. 7), so area 3. q3: learned baselines DDPG [49] and PPO [48]; the epsilon-greedy baseline has no neural network (p. 11) and is taken as the non-learned baseline, for the reviewer to confirm. Fig. 6 reports measured time cost per step (p. 11).
